Buying commercial fryers from China starts with a simple question: what do your customers actually fry, and what can their kitchens connect? A countertop electric fryer for a snack shop is a different purchase from a floor-standing gas fryer or a pressure fryer for chicken. This shortlist helps importers and wholesalers find the right enquiry route, compare factory-price quotations and plan a small first order. At DDNZ, we combine manufacturing and trade with model-specific low-MOQ supply proposals. Send us a reference machine and your destination; we can start without a finished technical specification.

  • Match the cooking job and local utilities before comparing prices.
  • Separate standard-machine, logo and printed-carton minimums.
  • Include replacement parts and repair support in the first enquiry.

Send DDNZ your fryer photos, destination and trial quantities.

1. Ten Chinese fryer manufacturers to shortlist

DDNZ wrote this guide and appears at No. 6 with its own fryer catalogue. The list is ordered for sourcing and comparison by application.

ManufacturerModel or configurationWhat to ask for

MARCHEFEFSJ-9 automatic-lift electric fryerMatch the exact SKU, lift motor and controller

JieguanGF-775 single-tank gas fryerSpecify the fitted gas valve and part number
KimcocinaEF-26 single tank / EF-26-2 twin tankCheck oil separation before pricing branding

HualingHDF-4 / HDF-4+4 countertop electric fryersVerify connections, plugs and supplied baskets
MIJIAGAOFE 3.6.75-L three-tank open fryerChoose open or pressure by cooking process

1. Shangbang. Compare the D and E configurations if you need separate oil for two menu items on the same counter. Put natural gas or LPG and the required inlet pressure on the RFQ. Ask for a dimensioned drawing that shows where each drain opens and whether a waste-oil container fits below.

2. MARCHEF. Start with the automatic-lift EFSJ-9 listing. The page headline and spec table use different suffixes, so have the supplier attach a model plate photo and signed spec to the quote. Ask for a video of the basket lifting your intended load, plus the motor and controller part numbers.

3. Meilern. Shortlist the F3-NG, F4-NG and F5-NG series for a gas line. Give each supplier the same food, batch weight, starting oil temperature and time between loads. Ask them to record how long the oil takes to recover across consecutive batches so you can size for the lunch rush.

4. Jieguan. Start with the GF-775 for a single oil circuit. If your dealer wants the Minisit valve, specify it as a line item and confirm the fitted valve reference. Have the local installer check the fuel, inlet pressure and connection before you approve the model.

5. Kimcocina. The EF-26 has one tank and two baskets. The EF-26-2 has two tanks and four baskets. If customers need separate oil, request the drain layout for the twin model before ordering it. Quote the standard machine, logo plate and printed cartons separately for your first order.

6. DDNZ Global. Our electric fryer range lists the ZH-101V with one 10 L tank and 3 kW rated input, and the ZH-102V with two 10 L tanks and 3 + 3 kW rated input. Those volumes describe the tanks. Ask for the working oil fill and usable basket load. For a small trial, send quantities by model, destination and power supply. We can quote the standard version and price logo, packing and starter spares separately. Have the local installer confirm the connection arrangement and site capacity with both tanks heating.

7. Hualing. Use the HDF-4 and HDF-4+4 to compare single- and twin-tank countertop versions. Ask for the actual electrical plate and the number of cords and plugs supplied. Request basket dimensions and a loaded test with both tanks running before approving the twin model.

8. MIJIAGAO. The FE 3.6.75-L is listed as a three-tank open fryer. For fries and breaded items, ask to see basket loading, drain routing and the oil filtration cycle on the quoted unit. For a pressure-fried chicken menu, request a separate pressure model quote with its gasket, lock and valve parts list.

9. Lestov / Qinxin. For a movable single-tank induction configuration, start with the LT-ZLII-E112. Verify the supply and the cable and caster arrangement where the machine will be used. Give the local service partner the induction module, cooling fan and temperature probe references before you order.

10. AT Cooker. The ZLT-A2S15 has two independently controlled tanks. Ask to see both sides heat under load, then check the total connected input and simultaneous operation with the local electrician. Request the controller and power board references for the quoted electrical version.

2. Gas or electric: buy the version your customers can install

For a gas fryer, specify LPG or natural gas, required inlet pressure and gas connection. Check whether that model also needs electricity for controls or filtration. For an electric fryer, specify voltage, frequency, phase and rated input. Induction is an electric option, with different service components from a resistance-heated fryer.

Suppose your dealers mainly sell to small takeaway shops. Before adding a larger floor-standing model, ask a local installer whether those shops can supply its power or gas and provide suitable extraction. A cheaper factory quotation loses its appeal when the customer cannot install the machine.

Request destination-appropriate documents for the exact model. IEC 60335-2-37 covers commercial electric fryer safety, but a reference to the standard is not a model certificate or permission to sell in every country. Have your importer or compliance adviser confirm the applicable local requirements.

Single tank, twin tank or split vat? Count the oil compartments before you count baskets. Two baskets in one tank share the same oil. A twin-tank model has two tanks in one chassis. Confirm whether each has separate heat controls and whether both can run at once on the available supply. A split-vat design divides a fryer vat into smaller cooking compartments. Check the usable basket size on each side, separate temperature settings, and whether the drain, filtration or oil return is shared.

Suppose a takeaway sells fries and breaded chicken at the same time. Ask the supplier to show the maximum usable batch for each basket and how the oil temperature recovers between successive loads. If the customer requires separate oil, verify the entire drain and return circuit as well as the tanks. For a buyer who mostly fries one product in larger batches, ask whether a full vat accommodates their usual load before specifying two smaller compartments.

3. Get a factory-price quotation you can compare

Use one enquiry sheet for every quotation:

Put this in the enquiryWhat the quotation should identify
Food, peak batch size and kitchen spaceOpen or pressure fryer, oil capacity per compartment, usable basket size and loaded recovery test
Gas or electrical supplyExact version, rated input and connections
Cleaning and operating preferencesDrain, controls, filtration and any lift mechanism
Trial quantity and brandingMachine MOQ, logo MOQ and carton MOQ separately
Destination and delivery basisExport packing, freight scope and excluded local charges
Repair arrangementsParts diagram, fitted part numbers, local dealer and who pays for freight and labour

Ask for prices at the trial quantity and your intended repeat quantity. Compare equipment, packing, starter parts, freight, import charges and installation as separate lines. We would rather build a useful first assortment than fill a container with too many untested variants.

DDNZ's integrated manufacturing-and-trade approach connects factory-price supply with an order sized around the chosen models. Low MOQ is confirmed by configuration, including branding and packing. Agree the production photographs, nameplate checks and pre-packing checks in the order, so you can review the goods against the approved sample.

4. Who supplies export spares and who comes to site?

Contact the manufacturer for parts. Send the model, serial number, nameplate photo and fault code or a photo of the failed part. Ask the factory to match the part to the production version and confirm the part number, availability, dispatch time and warranty terms. For the first shipment, ask for the parts diagram and price a starter kit for your exact models. A fryer with a lift mechanism or induction module needs a different kit from a basic electric fryer.

The local dealer arranges on-site service. The dealer or its service partner handles the site visit, diagnosis and fitting. For gas or pressure equipment, the dealer should send a qualified technician. Put replacement freight, call-out and labour charges in the warranty terms before paying. See the commercial kitchen spare-parts buying guide.

5. Questions before a first wholesale order

Which manufacturer has the lowest factory price?

Compare current quotations for the same configuration and order quantity. Start with the required fryer type, utilities and packing; then ask DDNZ for a factory-price proposal. A catalogue's lowest displayed figure cannot establish the cheapest delivered, usable machine.

Can I start with a low-MOQ trial order?

Ask for a standard-model trial first, with quantities per model. Confirm branding and printed packaging separately. DDNZ can discuss model-specific low-MOQ options; the quotation should state the accepted quantity and configuration before payment.

Can I change a gas fryer from LPG to natural gas locally?

Do not assume conversion is allowed. Order the correct gas version. If conversion is necessary, obtain the manufacturer's exact-model procedure and approved parts, and have a qualified technician check local requirements and carry out the work.

Does the fryer come with overseas repair service?

For an exported fryer, contact the manufacturer to identify and arrange replacement parts. The local dealer handles on-site diagnosis, repair and fitting. Confirm in writing who pays parts freight, the call-out fee and labour.

6. Send us the model you want to sell

Contact DDNZ on WhatsApp for a fryer trial proposal. Send your country and city, a machine photo or model, what your customers fry, gas or electrical supply if known, and quantities per model. Add any private-label and starter-parts requirements. We can use that brief to discuss factory-price supply and a first order you can build on.
